newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher as electronics rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher as electronics rise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished nearly one percent higher on Saturday, boosted by active buying in electronic stocks, brokers said.
The weighted index closed up 64.09 points, or 0.94 percent, at its intraday high of 6,889.19. Turnover was an active T$48.48 billion in the shortened Saturday session.

Electronic and machinery shares, which had undergone a correction, led the market to rise 1.84 percent. Acer Inc, the session's most actively traded stock, rose T$2, or 3.92 percent, to T$53, followed by A.S.E., which was up T$1.5, or 2.86 percent, to T$54.
"Confidence recovered after Taiwan share prices defied big donwturns in overseas markets in previous sessions," said Tsao Chung-ping, an analyst of Ting Kong Securities.
Brokers also attributed Saturday's gains partly to some institutions' year-end window dressing.

Plastics were also strong. Key members of the industrial giant Formosa group -- Nan Ya Plastics and Formosa Plastics -- were up T$1 or 1.53 percent to T$66.5 and T$1.5 or 2.17 percent to T$70.5 respectively.
The market is expected to gradually challenge the 7,000-point resistance level next week, with initial support seen at 6,800 points, brokers said.
